summary: Jeanne Bliss argues that beloved and prosperous companies share a trust-based operating model: they believe that customers can be trusted, they minimize wedges created by excessive rules, and they empower employees to act with autonomy. This results in Energy, innovation, and a workforce that brings its best self to work. A core theme is treating customers as assets with long-term value rather than as mere costs, and granting decision rights across the organization to nurture that asset. The video stitches these ideas to a concrete example—Zane Cycles offering test rides without collateral—to show how trust can coexist with risk, yielding a high lifetime value per customer (about $12,500). It closes by urging hiring for long-term values, not just filling seats, underscoring the link between personal ethics and business behavior.
title: Belief-Driven Customer Asset Strategy: Lessons from Jeanne Bliss on Beloved and Prosperous Companies
